item.title: Nintendo Shares Rise as ‘Pokopia’ Global Sales Top 5 Million
item.description: Nintendo Co. shares surged after global sales of its hit game Pokémon Pokopia topped 5 million units since its March launch, with some analysts saying the stock is back on its upward trajectory.

item.title: Tankers Are Going Dark for Longer to Get Oil Out of Middle East
item.description: Supertankers are going dark for longer to get oil through the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab el-Mandeb strait, doubling down on tactics honed in the earlier days of the Iran war.

item.title: South Africa Taps London to Boost Offshore Adoption of New Benchmark Rate
item.description: South Africa is working with the London Stock Exchange to convert outstanding derivative contracts linked to a soon-to-be-abandoned rand reference rate to the country’s new benchmark.

item.title: Philippine Central Bank Chief Eyes Less Aggressive Rate Hikes
item.description: The Philippine central bank will be less aggressive in raising its key interest rate as economic growth slows, according to Governor Eli Remolona.

item.title: Z.ai to Rival Anthropic, OpenAI in Coding With New AI Model
item.description: Z.ai Co. is set to upgrade its flagship AI model, adding to a series of Chinese open-weight offerings seeking to outcompete Anthropic PBC and OpenAI.

item.title: Africa’s Domestic Debt Outshines EM Peers as High-Yield Chase Intensifies
item.description: African local-currency debt is outperforming emerging-market peers, as high yields and economic reforms drive investor appetite for government securities.

item.title: ICICI Joins Indian Banks Chasing Dollar Loans, Swelling Demand
item.description: India’s ICICI Bank Ltd. has launched a syndicated offshore loan of about $1.45 billion, according to people familiar with the matter, joining a growing number of local banks tapping overseas debt to capitalize on a central bank facility that lowers hedging costs.

item.title: Trustar Is Said to Near $1.5 Billion Deal for Alibaba Gaming Arm
item.description: Asian private equity firm Trustar Capital is nearing a deal to acquire Alibaba Group Holding Ltd.’s video game business, according to people with knowledge of the matter.

item.title: EM Assets Buoyed by Easing US Rate Worries, Gains in AI Leaders
item.description: Emerging-market stocks and currencies gain as a retreat in a key US inflation measure strengthened hopes that the Federal Reserve may not have to raise interest rates soon.

item.title: Malaysia Revises Up Second-Quarter Growth to 6% With Central Bank Upbeat
item.description: Malaysia’s economy grew faster than initially estimated in the second quarter as stronger-than-expected exports tied to the artificial intelligence boom and steady domestic demand countered the impact of the war in the Middle East.

item.title: Russian Regions Report New Fuel Crunch As Kyiv Hits Refineries
item.description: Several regions of Russia are facing fuel shortages again after Ukraine resumed almost daily attacks on oil refineries in the country.

item.title: China Tech Earnings Renew Focus on Hardware Stocks Over Internet
item.description: Chinese tech firms’ early earnings are giving hardware stocks renewed momentum, while internet platforms still struggle to show a full consumer‑demand recovery.

item.title: Vietnam’s SCIC Plans Broad Divestment as FTSE Upgrade Nears
item.description: Vietnam’s state investment arm plans to exit dozens of companies over the next four years, freeing up capital and potentially boosting the supply of tradable shares as the country prepares for its elevation to emerging-market status.

item.title: Fast Money Bets on November RBA Hike in Fight Against Inflation
item.description: Speculative investors are increasingly betting the Reserve Bank of Australia will raise interest rates again in November as inflation remains above the central bank’s target.

item.title: Easing India Rupee Volatility May Help Attract More Foreign Money
item.description: The rupee has been steadier than the Indonesian rupiah and Philippine peso.

item.title: Australia Home Loans Fall Most Since Pandemic as Tax Changes Hit
item.description: Australian home buyers continued to borrow less, with new loans falling by the most since the pandemic as tax reforms and declining prices encouraged buyers to wait for signs of a bottom.

item.title: Japan Power Futures Get Boost as Utilities Hedge Price Risk
item.description: Power futures are becoming an increasingly popular tool for Japanese companies to manage risk arising from fuel-price volatility, with the number of short-term contracts traded on the nation’s biggest platform rising for four straight months.

item.title: Asian Memory Chipmakers Rise as Sandisk Outlook Lifts Confidence
item.description: Asian memory-chip stocks climbed, as a bullish outlook from Sandisk Corp. boosted optimism on longer term benefits from the artificial intelligence boom.

item.title: Alibaba, Baidu, Kuaishou Address Mounting AI Costs as Competition Intensifies
item.description: Alibaba Group Holding Ltd., Baidu Inc. and Kuaishou Technology are the next big names in tech that will have to address concerns over the mounting financial costs needed to sustain intense AI competition.

item.title: PBOC Conducts Mid-Month Overnight Reverse Repo for First Time
item.description: China’s central bank injected liquidity through overnight reverse repos on Friday, marking its first such operation in the middle of a month.

item.title: China’s High-Tech Boom Seen Failing to Halt Slowdown of Economy
item.description: China’s economy likely kicked off the second half of 2026 in much the same way it saw out the first, with a booming technology sector failing to make up for an historic investment slump and sluggish consumption.

item.title: Uber and China’s Pony AI to Deploy 2,000 Robotaxis in Europe
item.description: Pony AI Inc. said it plans to deploy more than 2,000 robotaxis across Europe in partnership with Uber Technologies Inc., accelerating the race to commercialize autonomous-mobility in the region.

item.title: Indian Startup Leans on Cancer-Sniffing Dogs and AI for Early Detection
item.description: On a two-acre farm outside Bengaluru in southern India, Billy, Jessie and Banu put on their gear, enter a laboratory packed with samples and clock in for a shift detecting early signs of cancer.

item.title: Thrive Investor Letter Reveals OpenAI-Fueled Growth, Stake Sale
item.description: Thrive Capital’s 2022 early-stage venture capital fund, a $516 million investment vehicle that made early bets on OpenAI, SpaceX and Anduril Industries Inc., has grown to be worth more than $3.7 billion as of the end of June.

item.title: Read Joshua Kushner’s First Formal Thrive Capital Investor Letter
item.description: In the absence of an investor day this year, Josh Kushner wrote his first formal letter to backers for his investment firm Thrive.

item.title: Japan Stocks Headed for Best Weekly Rise Since June on AI Gains
item.description: Japanese stocks are headed for their best weekly gain in about two months led by a tech rally after US wholesale inflation decelerated, easing concerns about immediate interest-rate increases by the Federal Reserve.

item.title: India Bar Council Retreats After ‘Cockroach’ Protest Threat
item.description: India’s national regulator for lawyers reversed an order barring an entire graduating class at one of the country’s leading law schools from enrolling as advocates, hours after the move triggered threats of protests from a fast-growing youth movement.

item.title: CXMT’s Absence Leaves CSI 300 Missing China’s Biggest Stock
item.description: China’s CSI 300 Index risks losing its appeal as the nation’s key benchmark until it includes memory giant CXMT Corp., an event that’s unlikely to happen until the end of 2027, according to Bloomberg Intelligence.

item.title: Carry Traders Exploit Intervention to Rebuild Yen Shorts
item.description: Every intervention to prop up the yen is also creating a fresh opportunity to sell it.
